Title: Add configurable source-read expansion and safe allow/deny policies for KB-linked tool requests.
Description:
Problem: when a KB entry points to a source file and line range, the tooling currently cannot clearly answer whether it may read nearby source context outside the exact quoted lines. That makes source-grounded answers less useful than they could be and leaves the safe read/write boundary underspecified for future automation.

Desired outcome: source-backed requests can optionally expand to nearby lines within a configured safe source-read scope, while tool writes remain strictly controlled by explicit approval and deny rules.

Scope:
- In scope: configurable safe directories for source reads, configurable safe directories for tool writes, allow/deny lists for read and write requests, an opt-in mode for broad read access, and task/tool behavior for answering whether surrounding source context may be read.
- In scope: clarifying behavior when the requested source location is outside the allowed read scope or when no surrounding read is permitted.
- Out of scope: automatic approval for any write request, and any change that bypasses human approval for durable writes.

Acceptance criteria:
- A source-linked request can state whether nearby context may be read from the same file and, if allowed, can expand to surrounding lines within the configured safe read scope.
- The tool/prompt path can clearly say when source-context expansion is not allowed.
- Config supports explicit safe read directories, explicit safe write directories, and allow/deny lists for both read and write requests.
- A broad-read opt-in exists, but write requests still never auto-approve.
- Dangerous or out-of-scope source reads and all unauthorized writes are rejected or blocked before execution.

Validation:
- Focused tests cover allowed nearby source reads, denied source reads, and denied writes.
- Focused tests cover the opt-in broad-read mode without enabling automatic write approval.
- Update any prompt or task-routing coverage needed to keep the user-facing answer consistent.

Notes:
- This is meant to preserve source-grounded usefulness while keeping the source-read and tool-write trust boundary explicit.
- Related precedent: the shared source-bridge/tool-risk task and the explicit write-approval tasks already in the backlog.

Comments.Body: Captured from a chat request about whether source-linked KB entries can expand to nearby source lines and how safe read/write boundaries should be configured. Broad reads may be opt-in, but writes must stay approval-gated.
